failures.workload: five-node four-Pythia-learner plus CPU-only syncer FineWeb-Edu capacity smoke

failure.summary: The authorized smoke timed out in the Stage 1 pytest preflight after exactly 264 tests completed; the Pythia/FineWeb learner and syncer workload never started.
failure.automatic_capture: The pre-walltime timeout returned 124 and the shared ERR trap wrote failures/raw-2393122.opbs-2307217.json before PBS walltime.

cause.summary: The active test was the concurrent global-authority reader/writer regression. AtomicGlobalCommitStore shared an unsynchronized per-process authority cache between readers and the writer; a reader could reinstall an older bound record between the writer's current-authority load and cache check, making commit raise. The test then hid that writer exception because its reader stop event was not set in a finally block, so executor shutdown waited until the external timeout.
direct_evidence: The partial quiet log contains exactly 264 completion dots. The last complete verbose suite at bac11ae identifies test 265 as test_concurrent_readers_observe_only_complete_committed_authorities, and the diff from bac11ae to the failed runtime adds tests only in lexically later S1-13 files, so the prefix order is unchanged.

The same regression had previously exposed an incomplete suite at this exact test boundary, but its earlier correction bounded retained observations without serializing AtomicGlobalCommitStore._authority_cache.

Code review shows load_fragment reads and writes _authority_cache without a lock, while commit separately loads current authority and later requires the cached object to be the identical object. A concurrent stale bound-record read can overwrite that cache entry during this interval.

The test set finished only after all 20 writer commits. Any writer exception therefore entered ThreadPoolExecutor shutdown while eight readers continued waiting for finished, masking the original exception as a hang.
Scheduler memory remained bounded at 5,647,744 KB and PBS reported no abnormal node, distinguishing this failure from the historical append-only observation-memory growth.
No mpirun log, role record, proposal, or gate output exists; failure occurred before the real-model workload launch.
cause.scope: The review found a thread-safety defect in the core in-process atomic-authority cache and a masking defect in its regression harness. Filesystem publication remains process-atomic, and no real learner/syncer execution occurred in this job.

changes: Protect AtomicGlobalCommitStore cache reads and the complete load-validate-publish-cache commit transaction with one reentrant per-instance lock.
Bound each concurrent reader's observation loop and set the reader stop event in a finally block so a writer exception is surfaced instead of converted into executor-shutdown timeout.
Add a deterministic two-thread regression that holds a writer immediately before visibility and proves a local reader cannot replace the cache until the commit completes.
Run the smoke pytest preflight with verbose node IDs, slow-test durations, and a faulthandler watchdog while retaining the 120-second external ceiling.
Keep the sequential smoke supervision ceiling at 1590 seconds plus at most 15 seconds terminal grace, preserving 195 seconds of PBS-walltime headroom.
